title: First trip west and King Oliver's Nine Kings in San Francisco
summary: Garland first came west in 1917, then returned in 1920 with King Oliver's band, with the lineup he lists, playing a dance hall in San Francisco and then Oakland.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: And when did you first come out the West Coast? Well, it's like I told you, the first time I come to the West Coast, when I was in Tennessee 10 in 17. 1917.
Then I come back again to the West Coast in 20, 21, no, 20, out to Frisco, to the Deluxe.

What band were you with then? King Oliver. King Oliver. King Oliver. King Oliver. King Oliver. King Oliver's Nine Kings. There were nine pieces? Nine. It's a pretty big band, huh? Well, we had Jimmy Ballard played violin and tempo for Oakland to What band were you with then? King Oliver. We went there with King Oliver's Nine Kings. There were nine pieces?
There were nine. It's a pretty big band, huh?
Well, we had Jimmy Pallar played violin and tenor saxophone, and we had Jones playing mellophone and alto.

David Jones playing alto, mellophone and sax. We had Johnny Dots playing clarinet. We had Lilian Armstrong on piano. We had Minor Hall on drums, and we had Notre Dutre on trombone, and myself on bass, and King Oliver was playing. That's the way the band was picked up when we went to Frisco, playing at the Procola dance hall.
And when you came west, did you plan to stay here, or did you just come for a short trip? Well, we come to play that engagement, that's all.

No, we come to play that engagement, and when the Procola fooled up, we went over to Oakland, and I got a job over there from Lucious for the band. Joe told me to go ahead, I did the band.
